# A uniform bound on all Báez-Duarte distances

Status: formalized (Lean, unconditional)
Date: 2026-08-09

## What is proved

`RHTower/UniformDistanceBound.lean`. Every earlier bound was for a single section. Monotonicity of the distance
in the family (`bdDist_mono`) upgrades the best single-generator bound to the whole sequence, because the
discrete section of length `N` contains the modulus `4` as soon as `N ≥ 4`:

**`bdDistDiscrete_sq_le_quarter` — `d_N² ≤ 1 − (log 2)²/(4·((3log 2)/8 − π/32))` for every `N ≥ 4`.**

This is the first statement here that constrains the *entire* sequence rather than one section, and it is
unconditional and symbolic.

## Why this is the ceiling of the method

The value is fixed — it does not improve with `N` — and it cannot be improved much by this route:

* by `SingleGeneratorUseless`, no single modulus gives a gain better than `O((log m)²/m)`, so no other choice of
  one generator beats `m = 4` by more than a constant;
* a bound uniform in `N` that *tended to `0`* would be `d_N → 0`, i.e. the Riemann hypothesis. So the only way
  past a fixed constant is the collective estimate that remains open. There is no unconditional theorem of this
  shape waiting to be found: an upper bound on the collective gain staying away from `1` for all `N` would
  refute RH, and a bound reaching `1` is RH.

The complementary floor is now proved in the same formulation, not only for step vectors:
`DistancePositivity.bdDistDiscrete_ge_factorial_floor` gives `√(1/(N!(N!+1))) ≤ d_N` and hence
`bdDistDiscrete_pos : 0 < d_N` for every `N`, by transporting the arithmetic obstruction through
`bdGen_bdDiscrete_eq_stepVec` and `bdTarget_eq_stepVec`.  So the picture is: each `d_N` is strictly positive,
the whole sequence sits below the constant above from `N = 4` on, and **whether the infimum is `0` is exactly
RH.**

That is where the lane ends unconditionally, and this card is the statement of it.

| `ZetaInvStripBound.lean` | the assembly — nine lines of tactic once the pieces exist |

each an independent atom. Supply `have : (2:ℝ)/L^2 = 2 * (1/L^2) := by ring` (and similarly for `3`)

## The exponent-one region, valid from height nine (2026-08-06)

`RHTower/Sieve/ZeroFreeRegionFromNine.lean : exists_zero_free_region_from_nine`, unconditional.

```lean
∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ β t : ℝ, 9 ≤ |t| → β ≤ 1 → 1 - c / Real.log |t| < β →
  riemannZeta ((β : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * Complex.I) ≠ 0
```

`exists_zero_free_region` has the right *shape* but only past `T = exp(u₀²)` with `u₀ ≥ 202` —
`exp(40804)`, unusable as stated. The corpus's **explicit** exponent-nine region
`RHTower.riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_re_gt_one_sub` (constant `1/(2·27·28·224⁴)`) is valid from `|t| ≥ 9`,
and on the *bounded* range `[9, T]` its width `c₉/log⁹|t|` dominates `c/log|t|` as soon as
`c ≤ c₉/log⁸T` (`kappa_one_of_kappa_nine`). Shrinking the constant therefore extends the
exponent-one shape down to height `9`.

The constant is tiny — `c₉/log⁸T` with `log T ≥ 40804` — but the shape and range of validity are
what a consumer needs; the two regions are complementary rather than competing, and this makes that
explicit.

**Literature note.** arXiv:2603.21490 (2026-03-23) proves `ζ(σ+it) ≠ 0` for `t ≥ 3` and
`σ ≥ 1 - 1/(4.896 log t)` — the same shape with an explicit constant of order `0.2` from height `3`.
Reproducing that needs explicit numerical estimates (mollifiers, explicit `ζ` bounds), which the
no-computation constraint rules out here; it is recorded as the sharp target, not as a gap.

## `ζ'/ζ` from height ten (2026-08-06)

`exists_logDeriv_zeta_bound` is now a corollary of

```lean

  (hregion : ∀ β γ', T₀ ≤ |γ'| → β ≤ 1 → 1 - c / Real.log |γ'| < β → riemannZeta (β + iγ') ≠ 0) :
  ∃ c' C, 0 < c' ∧ 0 < C ∧ ∀ σ γ, max 4 (T₀ + 1) ≤ |γ| → 1 - c'/log|γ| ≤ σ → σ ≤ 9/8 →
    ‖logDeriv riemannZeta (σ + iγ)‖ ≤ C * log|γ| ^ 2
```

— the region is now a *hypothesis*, and the threshold is exposed as `max 4 (T₀ + 1)` rather than
hidden existentially. Two instantiations:

* `exists_logDeriv_zeta_bound` — the asymptotic region, as before;
* `exists_logDeriv_zeta_bound_from_ten` — the from-nine region, giving threshold **10**.

Only the constant `C` degrades. **The threshold has to be exposed, not existential**, or the
instantiation cannot name it.

**The trade-off is real, and it does not propagate everywhere.** `exists_zero_free_region_from_nine`
buys its low threshold with a tiny constant `c ≈ c₉/log⁸T`. Any downstream result whose proof needs
`log|γ| ≥ k/c` inherits an even *worse* threshold than before — e.g.
`exists_neg_log_zeta_upper_strip`, which requires `L ≥ 5/c` for the thin disc to sit inside the
region. The `ζ'/ζ` bound is different: its proof needs only `L ≥ 1`-type conditions and `T₀ + 1`, so
swapping the region is a pure win there. Check for `1/c` conditions before substituting.

## The strip bound, multiplicatively (2026-08-06)

`RHTower/Sieve/ZetaLowerStripMultiplicative.lean : exists_zeta_lower_strip`, unconditional:

```lean
∃ c T : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ 4 ≤ T ∧ ∀ σ γ : ℝ, T ≤ |γ| →
  1 - 1 / Real.log |γ| ^ 2 ≤ σ → σ ≤ 1 + 1 / Real.log |γ| ^ 2 →
  c / Real.log |γ| ^ 2 ≤ ‖riemannZeta ((σ : ℂ) + (γ : ℂ) * Complex.I)‖
```

— the logarithmic bound exponentiated, with `7/4` weakened to the integer `2` so that no real power
is needed. This is the form a contour argument consumes.

Two points that the logarithmic statement hides:

* **`log‖ζ‖` needs `ζ ≠ 0` to be invertible.** In Lean `Real.log 0 = 0`, so `-log‖ζ‖ ≤ B` is
  *satisfied* by `ζ = 0` and carries no information there. The nonvanishing has to be supplied
  separately: `zeta_ne_zero_on_thin_strip` shows the strip sits inside the zero-free region, since
  its width `log^{-2}|γ|` is below `c₀/log|γ|` once `log|γ| > 1/c₀`.
* **The exponent is now exposed.** `exists_neg_log_zeta_upper` and
  `exists_neg_log_zeta_upper_strip` state `7/4` literally instead of hiding it behind `∃ K`;
  otherwise the weakening `7/4 ≤ 2` cannot even be stated by a consumer. Same lesson as the
  region's constant: **existentially quantifying a constant that the proof computes makes the
  result unusable downstream.**

/-- Certified pointwise `O(sqrt epsilon)` error estimate. -/
structure SqrtHomogenizationBound (X : Type*) where
  error : ℝ → X → ℝ
  magnitude : X → ℝ
  constant : ℝ
  constant_nonneg : 0 ≤ constant
  magnitude_nonneg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ magnitude x
  error_nonneg : ∀ ε x, 0 ≤ error ε x
  bound : ∀ {ε}, 0 ≤ ε → ∀ x,
    error ε x ≤ constant * Real.sqrt ε * magnitude x

/-- Squaring the paper's `O(sqrt epsilon)` estimate gives an `O(epsilon)` energy error. -/
theorem SqrtHomogenizationBound.sq_le (H : SqrtHomogenizationBound X)
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (x : X) :
    H.error ε x ^ 2 ≤ H.constant ^ 2 * ε * H.magnitude x ^ 2 := by
  have hbound := H.bound hε x
  have hmajorant : 0 ≤ H.constant * Real.sqrt ε * H.magnitude x :=
    mul_nonneg (mul_nonneg H.constant_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)) (H.magnitude_nonneg x)
  calc
    H.error ε x ^ 2 ≤ (H.constant * Real.sqrt ε * H.magnitude x) ^ 2 :=
      (sq_le_sq₀ (H.error_nonneg ε x) hmajorant).mpr hbound
    _ = H.constant ^ 2 * ε * H.magnitude x ^ 2 := by
      rw [mul_pow, mul_pow, Real.sq_sqrt hε]

end SquareRootRate

/-!
# Liouville's Theorem for Harmonic Functions on the Complex Plane

A bounded harmonic function on the complex plane is constant.
-/

public section

open Bornology Complex Real Set

variable
  {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]

-- Auxiliary version of Liouville's theorem, for real-valued harmonic functions on the complex
-- plane.
private theorem InnerProductSpace.bounded_harmonic_on_complex_plane_is_constant_aux (f : ℂ → ℝ)
    (h_harm : HarmonicOnNhd f univ) (h_bound : Bornology.IsBounded (range f)) :
    ∀ z w, f z = f w := by
  -- By assumption, there exists a holomorphic function $f$ such that $\Re(f) = u$.
  obtain ⟨F, hF_diff, hF_re⟩ := h_harm.exists_analyticOnNhd_univ_re_eq
  -- Since $g(z)$ is bounded, by Liouville's theorem, $g(z)$ is constant.
  suffices ∀ z w, Complex.exp (F z) = Complex.exp (F w) by grind
  apply Differentiable.apply_eq_apply_of_bounded
  · apply (differentiable_exp.comp (fun x ↦ (hF_diff x (mem_univ x)).differentiableAt))
  rw [isBounded_iff_forall_norm_le] at *
  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := h_bound
  use Real.exp M
  simp_all only [mem_range, norm_eq_abs, forall_exists_index, forall_apply_eq_imp_iff,
    norm_exp, exp_le_exp]
  rw [← hF_re] at hM
  grind

/--
**Liouville's theorem for harmonic functions on the complex plane** A bounded harmonic function on
the complex plane is constant.
-/
theorem InnerProductSpace.bounded_harmonic_on_complex_plane_is_constant (f : ℂ → E)
    (h_harm : HarmonicOnNhd f univ) (h_bound : IsBounded (range f)) :
    ∀ z w, f z = f w := by
  intro z w
  obtain ⟨ℓ, h₁ℓ, h₂ℓ⟩ := exists_dual_vector'' ℝ (f z - f w)
  rw [map_sub, RCLike.ofReal_real_eq_id, id_eq] at h₂ℓ
  have η₁ : Bornology.IsBounded (range (ℓ ∘ f)) := by
    simpa [range_comp] using IsBounded.image ℓ h_bound
  rw [← sub_eq_zero, ← norm_eq_zero, ← h₂ℓ]
  grind [bounded_harmonic_on_complex_plane_is_constant_aux (ℓ ∘ f) (h_harm.comp_CLM ℓ) η₁]

/-
# The exponential-polynomial fibre is closed under locally uniform limits

A family of exponentials of normalized bounded-degree polynomials, converging locally uniformly to
a limit that does not vanish at enough points, converges *as polynomials*: the derivative of the
limit divided by the limit is the limiting logarithmic derivative, the normalization pins the
constant term, and the finite-dimensional polynomial space is closed.  The limit function is again
the exponential of such a polynomial.

This is the closure statement behind a determinant completion: the polynomial factor of a
convergent family of finite-rank determinants converges to a polynomial factor of the same degree
bound.

Main results:
* `deriv_exp_polynomial` — the derivative of the exponential of a polynomial.
* `exists_poly_limit_of_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_exp` — **the fibre is closed**.
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.GeneralNodePolynomialLimit

open Filter Topology

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

theorem deriv_exp_polynomial (p : Polynomial ℂ) (x : ℂ) :
    deriv (fun z => Complex.exp (Polynomial.eval z p)) x
      = Complex.exp (Polynomial.eval x p) * Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.derivative p) :=
  ((p.hasDerivAt x).cexp).deriv

theorem differentiableOn_exp_polynomial (p : Polynomial ℂ) (U : Set ℂ) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (fun z => Complex.exp (Polynomial.eval z p)) U :=
  (Complex.differentiable_exp.comp p.differentiable).differentiableOn

/-- **The exponential-polynomial fibre is closed under locally uniform limits.** -/
theorem exists_poly_limit_of_tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_exp {J : ℕ} {U : Set ℂ} (hU : IsOpen U)
    {P : ℕ → Polynomial ℂ} (hdeg : ∀ n, (P n).natDegree ≤ J + 1)
    (hP0 : ∀ n, (P n).coeff 0 = 0) {G : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hconv : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
      (fun n z => Complex.exp (Polynomial.eval z (P n))) G atTop U)
    {v : Fin (J + 1) → ℂ} (hv : Function.Injective v) (hvU : ∀ i, v i ∈ U)
    (hG : ∀ i, G (v i) ≠ 0) :
    ∃ Q : Polynomial ℂ, Q.natDegree ≤ J + 1 ∧ Q.coeff 0 = 0 ∧
      (∀ h : ℕ, Tendsto (fun n => (P n).coeff h) atTop (nhds (Q.coeff h))) ∧
      ∀ z ∈ U, G z = Complex.exp (Polynomial.eval z Q) := by
  classical
  have hdiff : ∀ᶠ n in (atTop : Filter ℕ),
      DifferentiableOn ℂ (fun z => Complex.exp (Polynomial.eval z (P n))) U :=
    Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun n => differentiableOn_exp_polynomial (P n) U
  have hderiv := hconv.deriv hdiff hU
  have hsamples : ∀ i, Tendsto
      (fun n => Polynomial.eval (v i) (Polynomial.derivative (P n))) atTop
      (nhds (deriv G (v i) / G (v i))) := by
    intro i
    have hnum : Tendsto
        (fun n => deriv (fun z => Complex.exp (Polynomial.eval z (P n))) (v i)) atTop
        (nhds (deriv G (v i))) := hderiv.tendsto_at (hvU i)
    have hden : Tendsto (fun n => Complex.exp (Polynomial.eval (v i) (P n))) atTop
        (nhds (G (v i))) := hconv.tendsto_at (hvU i)
    have hquot := hnum.div hden (hG i)
    refine hquot.congr fun n => ?_
    show deriv (fun z => Complex.exp (Polynomial.eval z (P n))) (v i)
        / Complex.exp (Polynomial.eval (v i) (P n))
      = Polynomial.eval (v i) (Polynomial.derivative (P n))
    rw [deriv_exp_polynomial, mul_comm, mul_div_assoc,
      div_self (Complex.exp_ne_zero _), mul_one]
  obtain ⟨Q, hQdeg, hQ0, hQcoeff⟩ :=
    exists_limit_of_tendsto_derivative_samples_at hv hdeg hP0 hsamples
  refine ⟨Q, hQdeg, hQ0, hQcoeff, fun z hz => ?_⟩
  have h1 : Tendsto (fun n => Complex.exp (Polynomial.eval z (P n))) atTop (nhds (G z)) :=
    hconv.tendsto_at hz
  have h2 : Tendsto (fun n => Polynomial.eval z (P n)) atTop
      (nhds (Polynomial.eval z Q)) :=
    tendsto_eval_of_tendsto_coeff hdeg hQdeg hQcoeff z
  exact tendsto_nhds_unique h1 (Complex.continuous_exp.continuousAt.tendsto.comp h2)

end

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-
# The exponential-polynomial fibre is closed under pointwise limits with derivatives

The closure statement needs no uniform convergence: what the logarithmic derivative argument uses is
the value and the derivative of the family at finitely many points.  Stating it that way removes the
locally uniform hypothesis, which for a series-defined limit is exactly the hard part.

Main results:
* `exists_poly_limit_of_tendsto_exp_samples` — **the fibre is closed under pointwise convergence of
  values and derivatives at the nodes**.
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.ExpPolynomialFactorClosure

open Filter Topology

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- **The exponential-polynomial fibre is closed under pointwise convergence of values and
derivatives at the nodes.** -/
theorem exists_poly_limit_of_tendsto_exp_samples {J : ℕ}
    {P : ℕ → Polynomial ℂ} (hdeg : ∀ n, (P n).natDegree ≤ J + 1)
    (hP0 : ∀ n, (P n).coeff 0 = 0)
    {v : Fin (J + 1) → ℂ} (hv : Function.Injective v)
    {G D : Fin (J + 1) → ℂ}
    (hval : ∀ i, Tendsto (fun n => Complex.exp (Polynomial.eval (v i) (P n))) atTop (nhds (G i)))
    (hder : ∀ i, Tendsto
      (fun n => deriv (fun z => Complex.exp (Polynomial.eval z (P n))) (v i)) atTop (nhds (D i)))
    (hGne : ∀ i, G i ≠ 0) :
    ∃ Q : Polynomial ℂ, Q.natDegree ≤ J + 1 ∧ Q.coeff 0 = 0 ∧
      ∀ h : ℕ, Tendsto (fun n => (P n).coeff h) atTop (nhds (Q.coeff h)) := by
  classical
  have hsamples : ∀ i, Tendsto
      (fun n => Polynomial.eval (v i) (Polynomial.derivative (P n))) atTop
      (nhds (D i / G i)) := by
    intro i
    have hquot := (hder i).div (hval i) (hGne i)
    refine hquot.congr fun n => ?_
    show deriv (fun z => Complex.exp (Polynomial.eval z (P n))) (v i)
        / Complex.exp (Polynomial.eval (v i) (P n))
      = Polynomial.eval (v i) (Polynomial.derivative (P n))
    rw [deriv_exp_polynomial, mul_comm, mul_div_assoc,
      div_self (Complex.exp_ne_zero _), mul_one]
  exact exists_limit_of_tendsto_derivative_samples_at hv hdeg hP0 hsamples

end

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Preserves.Shapes.Terminal

/-!
# Exponential ideals

An exponential ideal of a Cartesian closed category `C` is a subcategory `D ⊆ C` such that for any
`B : D` and `A : C`, the exponential `A ⟹ B` is in `D`: resembling ring-theoretic ideals. We
define the notion here for inclusion functors `i : D ⥤ C` rather than explicit subcategories to
preserve the principle of equivalence.

We additionally show that if `C` is Cartesian closed and `i : D ⥤ C` is a reflective functor, the
following are equivalent.
* The left adjoint to `i` preserves binary (equivalently, finite) products.
* `i` is an exponential ideal.
-/

@[expose] public section


universe v₁ v₂ u₁ u₂

noncomputable section

namespace CategoryTheory

open Category

open scoped CartesianClosed

section Ideal

variable {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁} C] [Category.{v₁} D] {i : D ⥤ C}
variable (i) [CartesianMonoidalCategory C] [MonoidalClosed C]

/-- The subcategory `D` of `C` expressed as an inclusion functor is an *exponential ideal* if
`B ∈ D` implies `A ⟹ B ∈ D` for all `A`.
-/
class ExponentialIdeal : Prop where
  exp_closed : ∀ {B}, i.essImage B → ∀ A, i.essImage (A ⟹ B)
attribute [nolint docBlame] ExponentialIdeal.exp_closed

/-- To show `i` is an exponential ideal it suffices to show that `A ⟹ iB` is "in" `D` for any `A` in
`C` and `B` in `D`.
-/
theorem ExponentialIdeal.mk' (h : ∀ (B : D) (A : C), i.essImage (A ⟹ i.obj B)) :
    ExponentialIdeal i :=
  ⟨fun hB A => by
    rcases hB with ⟨B', ⟨iB'⟩⟩
    exact Functor.essImage.ofIso ((ihom A).mapIso iB') (h B' A)⟩

/-- The entire category viewed as a subcategory is an exponential ideal. -/
instance : ExponentialIdeal (𝟭 C) :=
  ExponentialIdeal.mk' _ fun _ _ => ⟨_, ⟨Iso.refl _⟩⟩

open MonoidalClosed

/-- The subcategory of subterminal objects is an exponential ideal. -/
instance : ExponentialIdeal (subterminalInclusion C) := by
  apply ExponentialIdeal.mk'
  intro B A
  refine ⟨⟨A ⟹ B.1, fun Z g h => ?_⟩, ⟨Iso.refl _⟩⟩
  exact uncurry_injective (B.2 (MonoidalClosed.uncurry g) (MonoidalClosed.uncurry h))

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
/-- If `D` is a reflective subcategory, the property of being an exponential ideal is equivalent to
the presence of a natural isomorphism `i ⋙ exp A ⋙ leftAdjoint i ⋙ i ≅ i ⋙ exp A`, that is:
`(A ⟹ iB) ≅ i L (A ⟹ iB)`, naturally in `B`.
The converse is given in `ExponentialIdeal.mk_of_iso`.
-/
def exponentialIdealReflective (A : C) [Reflective i] [ExponentialIdeal i] :
    i ⋙ ihom A ⋙ reflector i ⋙ i ≅ i ⋙ ihom A := by
  symm
  apply NatIso.ofComponents _ _
  · intro X
    haveI := Functor.essImage.unit_isIso (ExponentialIdeal.exp_closed (i.obj_mem_essImage X) A)
    apply asIso ((reflectorAdjunction i).unit.app (A ⟹ i.obj X))
  · simp [asIso]

/-- Given a natural isomorphism `i ⋙ exp A ⋙ leftAdjoint i ⋙ i ≅ i ⋙ exp A`, we can show `i`
is an exponential ideal.
-/
theorem ExponentialIdeal.mk_of_iso [Reflective i]
    (h : ∀ A : C, i ⋙ ihom A ⋙ reflector i ⋙ i ≅ i ⋙ ihom A) : ExponentialIdeal i := by
  apply ExponentialIdeal.mk'
  intro B A
  exact ⟨_, ⟨(h A).app B⟩⟩

end Ideal

section

variable {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁} C] [Category.{v₁} D]
variable (i : D ⥤ C)

/- This cannot be a local instance since it has free variables,
it can instead be used as a have when needed.
We assume `HasFiniteProducts D` as a hypothesis below, to avoid making this a local instance.
-/
theorem reflective_products [Limits.HasFiniteProducts C] [Reflective i] :
    Limits.HasFiniteProducts D := ⟨fun _ => hasLimitsOfShape_of_reflective i⟩

open MonoidalClosed MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
open Limits in
/-- Given a reflective subcategory `D` of a category with chosen finite products `C`, `D` admits
finite chosen products. -/
-- Note: This is not an instance as one might already have a (different) `CartesianMonoidalCategory`
-- instance on `D` (as for example with sheaves).
-- See note [reducible non-instances]
abbrev CartesianMonoidalCategory.ofReflective [CartesianMonoidalCategory C] [Reflective i] :
    CartesianMonoidalCategory D :=
  .ofChosenFiniteProducts
    ({ cone := Limits.asEmptyCone <| (reflector i).obj (𝟙_ C)
       isLimit := by
         apply isLimitOfReflects i

e [reducible non-instances]
abbrev CartesianMonoidalCategory.ofReflective [CartesianMonoidalCategory C] [Reflective i] :
    CartesianMonoidalCategory D :=
  .ofChosenFiniteProducts
    ({ cone := Limits.asEmptyCone <| (reflector i).obj (𝟙_ C)
       isLimit := by
         apply isLimitOfReflects i
         apply isLimitChangeEmptyCone _ isTerminalTensorUnit
         letI : IsIso ((reflectorAdjunction i).unit.app (𝟙_ C)) := by
           have := reflective_products i
           refine Functor.essImage.unit_isIso ⟨terminal D, ⟨PreservesTerminal.iso i |>.trans ?_⟩⟩
           exact IsLimit.conePointUniqueUpToIso (limit.isLimit _) isTerminalTensorUnit
         exact asIso ((reflectorAdjunction i).unit.app (𝟙_ C)) })
  fun X Y ↦
    { cone := BinaryFan.mk
        ((reflector i).map (fst (i.obj X) (i.obj Y)) ≫ (reflectorAdjunction i).counit.app _)
        ((reflector i).map (snd (i.obj X) (i.obj Y)) ≫ (reflectorAdjunction i).counit.app _)
      isLimit := by
        apply isLimitOfReflects i
        apply IsLimit.equivOfNatIsoOfIso (pairComp X Y _) _ _ _ |>.invFun
          (tensorProductIsBinaryProduct (i.obj X) (i.obj Y))
        fapply BinaryFan.ext
        · change (reflector i ⋙ i).obj (i.obj X ⊗ i.obj Y) ≅ (𝟭 C).obj (i.obj X ⊗ i.obj Y)
          letI : IsIso ((reflectorAdjunction i).unit.app (i.obj X ⊗ i.obj Y)) := by
            apply Functor.essImage.unit_isIso
            haveI := reflective_products i
            use Limits.prod X Y
            constructor
            apply Limits.PreservesLimitPair.iso i _ _ |>.trans
            refine Limits.IsLimit.conePointUniqueUpToIso (limit.isLimit (pair (i.obj X) (i.obj Y)))
              (tensorProductIsBinaryProduct _ _)
          exact asIso ((reflectorAdjunction i).unit.app (i.obj X ⊗ i.obj Y)) |>.symm
        · simp only [BinaryFan.fst, Cone.postcompose, pairComp]
          simp [← Functor.comp_map, ← NatTrans.naturality_assoc]
        · simp only [BinaryFan.snd, Cone.postcompose, pairComp]
          simp [← Functor.comp_map, ← NatTrans.naturality_assoc] }

variable [CartesianMonoidalCategory C] [Reflective i] [MonoidalClosed C]
  [CartesianMonoidalCategory D]

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- If the reflector preserves binary products, the subcategory is an exponential ideal.
This is the converse of `preservesBinaryProductsOfExponentialIdeal`.
-/
instance (priority := 10) exponentialIdeal_of_preservesBinaryProducts
    [Limits.PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete Limits.WalkingPair) (reflector i)] :
    ExponentialIdeal i := by
  let ir := reflectorAdjunction i
  let L : C ⥤ D := reflector i
  let η : 𝟭 C ⟶ L ⋙ i := ir.unit
  let ε : i ⋙ L ⟶ 𝟭 D := ir.counit
  apply ExponentialIdeal.mk'
  intro B A
  let q : i.obj (L.obj (A ⟹ i.obj B)) ⟶ A ⟹ i.obj B := by
    apply MonoidalClosed.curry (ir.homEquiv _ _ _)
    apply _ ≫ (ir.homEquiv _ _).symm ((ihom.ev A).app (i.obj B))
    exact prodComparison L A _ ≫ (_ ◁ (ε.app _)) ≫ inv (prodComparison _ _ _)
  have : η.app (A ⟹ i.obj B) ≫ q = 𝟙 (A ⟹ i.obj B) := by
    dsimp
    rw [← curry_natural_left, curry_eq_iff, uncurry_id_eq_ev, ← ir.homEquiv_naturality_left,
      ir.homEquiv_apply_eq, Category.assoc, Category.assoc,
      prodComparison_natural_whiskerLeft_assoc, ← whiskerLeft_comp_assoc,
      ir.left_triangle_components, whiskerLeft_id, Category.id_comp]
    apply IsIso.hom_inv_id_assoc
  haveI : IsSplitMono (η.app (A ⟹ i.obj B)) := IsSplitMono.mk' ⟨_, this⟩

variable [ExponentialIdeal i]

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
/-- If `i` witnesses that `D` is a reflective subcategory and an exponential ideal, then `D` is
itself Cartesian closed.

To allow for better control of definitional equality, this construction
takes in an explicit choice of lift of the essential image of `i` to `D`, in the form of a functor
`l : i.EssImageSubcategory ⥤ D` and natural isomorphism `φ : l ⋙ i ≅ i.essImage.ι`. When
`l ⋙ i` is defeq to `i.essImage.ι`, images of exponential objects in `D` under `i` will be defeq
to the respective exponential objects in `C`. -/
@[implicit_reducible]
def cartesianClosedOfReflective' (l : i.EssImageSubcategory ⥤ D) (φ : l ⋙ i ≅ i.essImage.ι) :
    MonoidalClosed D where
  closed := fun B =>
    { rightAdj := i.essImage.lift (i ⋙ ihom (i.obj B))
        (fun X ↦ ExponentialIdeal.exp_closed (i.obj_mem_essImage X) _) ⋙ l
      adj := by
        apply (ihom.adjunction (i.obj B)).restrictFullyFaithful i.fullyFaithfulOfReflective
          i.fullyFaithfulOfReflective
        · symm
          refine NatIso.ofComponents (fun X => ?_) (fun f => ?_)
          · haveI :=
              Adjunction.rightAdjoint_preservesLimits.{0, 0} (reflectorAdjunction i)
            apply asIso (prodComparison i B X)
          · dsimp [asIso]
            rw [prodComparison_natural_whiskerLeft]
        · exact (i.essImage.liftCompιIso _ _).symm.trans <|
